messages.content: Portland is handled. New one: Columbia Basin water district wants me onsite for a nitrate analyzer skid startup. Tuesday safety briefing is 7:00 a.m., and there may be a Wednesday afternoon SCADA acceptance walk-through if the electrician gets terminations done. I need Monday Bay Area to Pasco options, but also compare Spokane plus the drive. Do not book yet.

Got it. I will compare Pasco against Spokane and include rental-car timing and a hotel shortlist near Richland or Kennewick. What Monday are we using, and should I start with SFO or include OAK/SJC if they materially improve the schedule?
Monday the 17th. Start with SFO. OAK or SJC only if they clearly beat it. I would rather leave after lunch than at dawn, but the Tuesday 7:00 safety briefing is the thing to protect.

For Monday the 17th, SFO is the better starting point. Here are the workable paths:

1. Best fit so far: SFO to Pasco via Seattle, departing about 1:30 p.m., 1 hour 15 minute connection, arriving Pasco around 6:10 p.m. Rental car pickup by roughly 6:45, Richland hotel around 7:15. This leaves time for dinner and sleep before the 7:00 a.m. briefing.

2. Acceptable backup: SFO to Pasco via Denver, departing about 12:50 p.m., arriving around 7:35 p.m. Connection is comfortable, but it pushes the hotel arrival later.

3. Spokane comparison: SFO to Spokane nonstop around 5:05 p.m., arriving about 7:20 p.m. Rental car by 7:50, then about 2 hours 15 minutes to Richland. Realistic hotel arrival is 10:15-10:30 p.m. Cleaner flight, worse night-before-site logistics.
That Spokane arrival is later than I wanted. But if the Pasco connection is fragile, I do not want to strand myself in Seattle. Is the 1:15 connection enough?

I would treat the Seattle connection as comfortable enough, not tight. Same carrier, normal domestic connection, and there is a later Seattle-Pasco flight as a recovery option if the first leg slips. The Denver option has a similar buffer but arrives later and gives you less time Monday night. Spokane avoids a connection but replaces it with a long nighttime drive across the basin.
Okay. Add a rental car read on both airports. I will have a Pelican case and maybe a small tote, so compact SUV is probably safer than a sedan.

Rental car read:

Pasco: compact SUV pickup around 6:40-6:50 p.m. is straightforward. The airport is small, so the timing is predictable. Drive to central Richland is about 20-25 minutes.

Spokane: compact SUV pickup around 7:45-8:00 p.m. should also work, but the long drive after pickup is the weak point. You would be doing most of the Spokane-to-Richland drive after dark.

For the gear, compact SUV is the right size. I would not drop to economy sedan unless price is a real issue.

Good. Hotel should be Richland or Kennewick, parking included or at least easy, and not some tired 3.2 review place. I need dinner nearby Monday night and the room basics for early starts, coffee and a fridge if possible.

Shortlist:

1. Hampton Inn Richland/Tri-Cities - best operational fit. Guest rating around 4.4, free parking, breakfast starts early, rooms list coffee maker and mini-fridge, and it is near the riverfront/downtown Richland dinner spots. Good for the Tuesday 7:00 start.

2. Homewood Suites by Hilton Richland - acceptable backup if you want more room. Rating around 4.3, free parking, breakfast, kitchen setup with refrigerator and coffee. Slightly more expensive, but very practical for a multi-night site stay.

3. SpringHill Suites Kennewick Tri-Cities - solid backup if the site activity shifts toward Kennewick. Rating around 4.4, parking, breakfast, restaurants around the convention-center area. Less ideal if most of your time is at the Richland-side district facilities.

Put Hampton Richland as the lead unless the rate is ridiculous. Homewood backup. I may need to inspect the equipment crate Monday evening if receiving signs for it. Can the Pasco plan still allow that?

Yes, if receiving or the contractor trailer can give you access Monday evening. With the Pasco arrival, you could be in Richland around 7:15 p.m. and likely at the trailer around 7:35-7:45 if it is nearby. That is tight but possible. With Spokane, crate inspection Monday night becomes unrealistic unless someone stays very late.
Crate status is the big unknown. It might not clear receiving until Monday. The Wednesday controls review is also tentative. Keep the plan flexible around those.

Then I would not book prepaid hotel or restrictive rental yet. Flight-wise, the Pasco one-stop is still the best fit because it protects Tuesday morning and gives you at least a chance at the Monday crate check. Spokane is the acceptable backup only if the Pasco fare jumps, the connection degrades, or the crate check becomes irrelevant.
What about return? If the controls walk-through happens Wednesday afternoon, I could probably fly home Thursday. If it slips, I may need Thursday morning.

For now I would hold the return decision. Thursday has workable Pasco-to-SFO one-stop options after lunch, including a mid-afternoon departure through Seattle and another through Salt Lake City. If the walk-through stays Wednesday afternoon, those are easy. If it slips to Thursday morning, the mid-afternoon options still might work, but I would want the exact acceptance window before booking the return.
So saved lead is Monday SFO to Pasco through Seattle, compact SUV, Hampton Richland. Spokane nonstop is not dead, but only as a backup. Correct?

Correct. Saved, not booked:

Lead plan: Monday SFO-Pasco via Seattle, afternoon departure, comfortable connection, arrive around 6:10 p.m.; compact SUV at Pasco; Hampton Inn Richland/Tri-Cities as the lead hotel.

Acceptable backup: Monday SFO-Spokane nonstop, then compact SUV and the longer drive to Richland, mainly if Pasco becomes unreliable or overpriced.

Open items: crate receiving/access Monday evening, whether the Wednesday SCADA acceptance walk-through stays on the calendar, and the final Thursday return window.

messages.content: Update on Columbia Basin: the crate is confirmed for Monday receiving. Electrician moved the SCADA acceptance walk-through to Thursday morning, and they want Wednesday open for calibration data. Narrow the outbound and tell me if Thursday return still works.

That makes the Pasco plan stronger. The Monday SFO-Pasco option through Seattle gets you into Pasco around 6:10 p.m., into a compact SUV by about 6:45, and to Richland around 7:15. That supports a Monday evening crate look if the trailer is open.

The Spokane nonstop still avoids a connection, but it likely puts you at the Richland hotel after 10:00 p.m. and leaves very little margin before Tuesday's 7:00 a.m. safety briefing.
What exactly is the connection buffer on the Pasco option? I do not want a 40-minute sprint.

The Seattle connection is about 1 hour 15 minutes. I would keep that one. There is also a Salt Lake routing with roughly 1 hour 20 minutes, but it arrives later. I would avoid the shorter Denver connection I saw because it adds stress without improving the arrival.
Then lead with the Seattle-Pasco version. Any reason to reconsider Spokane besides nonstop?

Only two reasons: if the Pasco fare changes sharply, or if the Seattle-Pasco segment becomes unavailable. Otherwise Spokane is a worse operational fit: longer drive, later hotel arrival, no realistic Monday crate inspection, and less rest before plant access.
Hotel direction: keep me in Richland unless Kennewick is substantially easier. Confirm Hampton details: breakfast timing, parking, room coffee, mini-fridge, and dinner within a short drive.

Hampton Inn Richland/Tri-Cities still looks like the lead. It shows free parking, breakfast beginning at 6:00 a.m., in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge listed, and several dinner options within a short drive along the riverfront or downtown Richland. Guest rating is about 4.4.

Homewood Richland remains the acceptable backup if you want a larger room or more refrigerator space. Kennewick does not look better unless the site work shifts that direction.
Good. Thursday acceptance is supposed to be morning, but I do not have the exact time. I would prefer not to race straight from the plant to PSC.

Then I would target a Thursday departure after 2:30 p.m. The cleaner return options are:

- Pasco to SFO via Seattle around 2:45 p.m., arriving SFO early evening. Best fit if acceptance ends by late morning.
- Pasco to SFO via Salt Lake City around 3:25 p.m., arriving later in the evening. Acceptable backup with a bit more buffer.
- Later Pasco-Seattle routing after 5:00 p.m., safest if the walk-through expands, but it gets you home noticeably later.
If acceptance is 8:30 to 10:30, the 2:45 return is fine. If they slide to noon, I need the 3:25 or later. Is that the right read?

Yes. If the window is 8:30-10:30, the 2:45 p.m. return gives room for wrap-up, a quick lunch, rental car return, and normal airport timing. If acceptance starts closer to noon, I would not use 2:45; I would move to the 3:25 or the later Seattle option.

Save it that way. Lead outbound is SFO-Pasco through Seattle on Monday afternoon. Hotel is Hampton Richland. Compact SUV. Return target is Thursday after 2:30, exact flight pending the acceptance time. Still do not book.

Saved, not booked. Best fit is Monday SFO-Pasco via Seattle with the 1 hour 15 minute connection, compact SUV at Pasco, and Hampton Inn Richland/Tri-Cities. Spokane nonstop remains backup only if Pasco falls apart.

For return, I have Thursday after 2:30 p.m. as the target. Use the 2:45 p.m. Pasco return if acceptance is truly 8:30-10:30; use 3:25 p.m. or later if the acceptance window moves toward midday.

messages.content: Columbia Basin is ready to book. SCADA acceptance is locked Thursday 8:30 to 10:30. Plant says I can inspect the crate Monday evening through the contractor trailer. Book the Pasco plan, not Spokane.

I have the Pasco plan ready: Monday afternoon SFO-Pasco via Seattle, compact SUV at Pasco, Hampton Inn Richland/Tri-Cities, and Thursday mid-afternoon Pasco-SFO via Seattle after the acceptance walk-through. Should I use the refundable hotel rate if the gap is modest, and select window seats where available?
Yes. Refundable hotel unless it is a huge spread. Economy is fine. Windows if available.
Refundable is only $18 more per night, so I would use it for this site visit. I will add a quiet-room request and note coffee maker and mini-fridge even though the room listing shows them.
Good. Book it. Add the Monday crate check, Tuesday 7:00 safety briefing, Wednesday calibration data day, and Thursday acceptance to the trip notes.

Booked. Flights are Monday SFO-Pasco via Seattle, departing about 1:30 p.m. and arriving Pasco about 6:10 p.m.; Thursday Pasco-SFO via Seattle, departing about 2:45 p.m. and arriving SFO early evening. Economy seats selected with windows where available: 12A outbound first leg, 8A outbound second leg, 9A return first leg, and 14A return second leg.
And rental and hotel are confirmed?

Confirmed. Compact SUV at Pasco for Monday evening pickup and Thursday return. Hampton Inn Richland/Tri-Cities is booked Monday through Thursday checkout on the refundable king rate, with quiet-room request and room notes for coffee maker and mini-fridge. Trip notes now show Monday evening crate inspection, Tuesday 7:00 a.m. safety briefing, Wednesday calibration data, and Thursday 8:30-10:30 SCADA acceptance.
